ateret-zekenim/part-001.txt.2:א: And one ate etc., or drank a cup that contains a revi'it etc.; and some say we do not require a kazayit for a revi'it (Kol Bo).
ateret-zekenim/part-001.txt.2:ב: But six do not; and not as Agur who wrote in the name of Or Zaru'a that they combine.
ateret-zekenim/part-001.txt.3:_: The one who joins must etc.; and nevertheless, even though he did not eat with them but only drank, he can say "Blessed are You... who has fed us from His bounty," for drinking is included in eating (Tosafot chapter "three who ate" and Mordechai).

baer-heitev/part-001.txt.1:_: With them. Bach wrote it is a mitzvah that they wash hands and bless haMotzi and eat a little because of zimun. See Shakh and Ateret Zekenim.
baer-heitev/part-001.txt.2:א: They combine. And if he already recited the final blessing he cannot again invite zimun with them, for he already departed from them; and some say for siman 194 seif 1 that there at least he ate bread. Magen Avraham.
baer-heitev/part-001.txt.2:ב: In brine. And nevertheless he requires a measure.
baer-heitev/part-001.txt.2:ג: Water. And Magen Avraham disagrees and rules that even with water he combines.
baer-heitev/part-001.txt.3:א: Of these. For birkat hamazon does not discharge the blessing of Borei nefashot rabot. And on wine it implies in Beit Yosef that he is discharged by birkat hamazon, and with wine too one does zimun; see siman 208 seif 17 that the same applies to dates; and see Taz siman 174 s.k. 8 who wrote that with our beer one certainly does zimun; and nevertheless l'chatchila he should intend not to be discharged by birkat hamazon. Magen Avraham.
baer-heitev/part-001.txt.3:ב: It helps. And specifically a kazayit. Magen Avraham.
baer-heitev/part-001.txt.3:ג: To drink. And Bach wrote his rabbis were accustomed to give him to drink if he did not want to eat, and he combines; and so is the custom now.
baer-heitev/part-001.txt.4:א: Satiety. Beit Yosef wrote that if each blesses to himself in a whisper and only they invite zimun, one who ate a kazayit can bless even if all know how to bless. See Lechem Ketanot part 2 siman 477 and see Yad Aharon. One who eats coarse eating—meaning he did not need that eating—discharges others in birkat hamazon if his throat enjoyed it. Shulchan Gavoah; and see Kenesset HaGedolah.
baer-heitev/part-001.txt.4:ב: Who drank. And if some ate to satiety and did not drink, and some did not eat to satiety and drank, it is better they bless over those who ate to satiety. Magen Avraham in the name of Peri Megadim.

beer-hagolah/part-001.txt.1:ב: Responsum of Rashba from that in Chullin 106.
beer-hagolah/part-001.txt.3:א: R' Yechiel in the name of his father the Rosh.
beer-hagolah/part-001.txt.3:ג: Rif and Rashba per the Yerushalmi.
beer-hagolah/part-001.txt.3:ד: Tosafot and Rosh and Rabbeinu Yonah.
beer-hagolah/part-001.txt.3:ה: In Hagahot Maimoniot there in the name of R' Meir.
beer-hagolah/part-001.txt.4:_: The Rosh and as the view of R' Yerucham.

beur-hagra/part-001.txt.1:_: Seif 1—and he is etc. Tosafot there s.v. ilu and as written in the printed edition; and Tosafot Berachot 42a s.v. immediately etc.; and this is what is written "and washing hands" etc.
beur-hagra/part-001.txt.2:א: Seif 2—kazayit etc. Mordechai; and it appears he learned from what is written "nine who ate" etc., that the one who is not divided from them is only in the species he eats—vegetable—but in measures they are equal; but it requires study, for we say there one dried fig and it is less than a kazayit in what is written in the first chapter of Shabbat 10, and they also said there regarding vegetable.
beur-hagra/part-001.txt.2:ב: That contains a revi'it. Mordechai, and as his view as above.
beur-hagra/part-001.txt.2:ג: And he is etc. There R' Yitzchak: Beit Shammai hold one who acts for himself etc.—a kazayit of grain etc.; and Rambam explained this is bread over which one blesses birkat hamazon; and in the Rosh there he is uncertain about this.
beur-hagra/part-001.txt.2:ד: But six etc. As our text: six certainly etc.; not like Rashi who complained about this.
beur-hagra/part-001.txt.3:א: Seif 3—the one who joins etc. See siman 177 seif 2 and the matters that follow etc., that haMotzi and birkat hamazon are not etc.—all the more so this one who did not eat bread at all; and as one who goes to the market, 45b, that they call to him etc. that he returns and blesses birkat hamazon for himself; and that which Shimon ben Shetach—because he judges in birkat hamazon he discharges him—as written siman 208 seif 17. Rashba.
beur-hagra/part-001.txt.3:ב: But for three etc. And some say that with vegetables etc. As with ten, for there 45 ruled like Mar Zutra that ten are stricter than three; and further from what is written "to discharge the many" etc. it implies specifically to discharge; and further in Yerushalmi there he said explicitly even with two; and the first view holds that only regarding sitting together we are stricter with ten, but otherwise we say there on the contrary etc.; and so there 47b R' Avahu: and even though etc.; and siman 196 seif 10 in the name of R' Hai Gaon; and from Yerushalmi 40 the reverse of what we say there—it teaches there: and he reclined and ate with them—even though he did not eat a kazayit of grain they invite zimun—the words of the Sages; R' Yaakov bar Acha in the name of R' Yochanan: they never invite zimun upon him until he eats a kazayit of grain; and it was taught: two bread and one vegetable combine—the baraita is like Rashbag; and Tosafot there s.v. nine etc.; and the last view holds that that Yerushalmi argues on our gemara, for there R' Yochanan argues on Rashbag, and in our gemara they answer "joining" etc.; and so that baraita that teaches there etc. is Rashbag etc.; and there is no distinction between three and ten, and R' Yochanan holds in all of them he does not combine.
beur-hagra/part-001.txt.3:ג: And some say that with a kazayit etc. As written in the Yerushalmi cited above; and above seif 2 Rambam explained bread—and this is the first view here, which is Rambam's view.
beur-hagra/part-001.txt.3:ד: Therefore etc. and if etc. Hagahot Maimoniot in the name of the Rambam.
beur-hagra/part-001.txt.4:א: Seif 4—companions etc. mitzvah etc. For they are obligated only d'rabbanan, as written 20b, and there a curse comes etc.
beur-hagra/part-001.txt.4:ב: And if there are not etc. Tosafot 48a s.v. until etc.; and nevertheless l'chatchila one should conduct per Beit HaGadol and as written in Yerushalmi: every mitzvah from which a person is exempt—he discharges the many with it—except birkat hamazon; and we taught: whoever is not obligated in a matter does not discharge the many with it—one who is obligated discharges; R' Elai said: birkat hamazon is different, as it is written "and you shall eat and be satisfied and bless"—one who ate blesses; but the Rosh wrote it is merely an asmakhta and it is d'rabbanan.
beur-hagra/part-001.txt.4:ג: And some say etc. For we hold like R' Meir, as written end of siman 196; and we say 45b that for R' Meir "and you were satisfied" refers to drinking; and Tosafot s.v. R' Meir and as written in Shulchan Aruch—and therefore Shulchan Aruch omitted it.
beur-hagra/part-001.txt.4:ד: And it is good etc. As above.

biur-halacha/part-001.txt.1:א: They can eat from it—thus is the reading in old editions of Shulchan Aruch, and the intent is specifically if both can eat from it; and so it implies from Rambam's wording; and therefore it is obvious that if one washed hands [or clearly diverted his mind that he would not eat anything, per what we wrote in siman 179 in Biur Halacha s.v. ve'afilu, and even per Beit Meir] automatically the third cannot join; and I found in Eliyah Rabbah that he too sides thus for the law, but afterward he is somewhat uncertain; and from the text of Chot Yair in Rif who reads "if they would bring me ardilia" etc. it also implies as we wrote; afterward I found in Ma'amar Mordechai who wrote clearly as our words, and he greatly wondered at Eliyah Rabbah who is uncertain—see there.
biur-halacha/part-001.txt.1:ב: He joins with them—meaning they are obligated in zimun [and it is not optional], and as the Mechaber ruled in siman 193 that it depends on finishing the meal, and this too is called finishing a meal; it implies from several poskim who ruled thus for the law, and not like Rabbeinu Yonah who holds this passage is only regarding optional zimun; and so it implies there in Rashi s.v. akilna that they are obligated in zimun. And know further that it implies from the Rishonim that this third can invite and discharge them from zimun as well.
biur-halacha/part-001.txt.1:ג: But if they said etc.—see Magen Avraham that per the second view explained above in siman 179 seif 1, "hav lan venevarekh" too is not complete diversion of mind regarding eating; therefore here they combine—all who have not washed mayim acharonim; and so it implies in several Acharonim [see Derishah and Eliyah Rabbah and Beur HaGra above in siman 179 seif 1] that this depends on that; however in Shulchan Aruch HaGraz tends to say our law is for everyone—see there his reason; and see Peri Megadim who also wants to side thus, and he left it requiring further study.
biur-halacha/part-001.txt.1:ד: He does not join—see Or Zaru'a who wants to innovate that this is specifically when there were two and a third came; but where three ate and were already obligated in zimun and again one came and ate a kazayit—even if they washed hands or said "hav lan venevarekh"—he also joins with them and invites for them and discharges them from the obligation of zimun; and with this is resolved what the Rishonim challenged [see Pesachim 103b Tosafot s.v. keivan] from that of Shimon ben Shetach—see there; however from other Rishonim who explained otherwise it implies they do not hold thus.
biur-halacha/part-001.txt.1:ה: With them—see Peri Megadim who sides that in zimun of three, wherever there is doubt for the law they combine [meaning it is permitted for them to invite]; but in zimun of ten where there is mention of the Name he is uncertain whether it is permitted because of the severity of "do not take [the Name in vain]"; and so Chayei Adam tends.
biur-halacha/part-001.txt.1:ו: And washing etc.—see Magen Avraham s.k. 3 what he brought in the name of Bach and I did not copy it, for Eliyah Rabbah already challenged it and it is brought in Sha'arei Teshuvah; and see Taz siman 193 s.k. 8 who also holds like Eliyah Rabbah's view.
biur-halacha/part-001.txt.2:א: Kazayit of vegetable—and in Beur HaGra it implies his view that we do not require a kazayit for joining ten; and so it implies in Chiddushei HaRa'ah, for he brings proof for Rif's ruling that specifically for ten one combines—from the Mishnah that teaches "they invite zimun until a kazayit," and our Mishnah deals with joining three—see there; behold it is proven that joining for ten is even with less than a kazayit; and in Shibolei Leket he also brings proof from Tosefta that for joining ten it helps even with less than a kazayit of grain—see there; and ostensibly the same applies to less than a kazayit of vegetable [and it is possible that even for grain one does not bless any final blessing on less than a kazayit, nevertheless it is considered more than vegetable; and in any case for grain his view is clear that even less than a kazayit helps]; and nevertheless in practice it requires study to be lenient against Shulchan Aruch's view, for Mordechai—from whom Shulchan Aruch took its source as explained in Beit Yosef—is not a lone view, for it is reasonable that all these poskim who do not distinguish between three and ten for joining hold thus, that in any case we require the measure of a kazayit—for behold it states in the Mishnah at the beginning of "three who ate" that the attendant who ate less than a kazayit—they do not invite zimun upon him; for even if we say per their explanation—even with any vegetable—it is proven from this in any case that we require specifically a kazayit even for joining [as all Rishonim explained that this Mishnah deals with joining]; and per them certainly one should not distinguish between three and ten [as is proven from the proof those who hold this view brought from "one of them went to the market," for on the contrary with ten we are stricter]; and if so certainly one should not be lenient per them with less than a kazayit even for ten; and since we came to this, why should we say that per Rif and his supporters who are stricter regarding joining, they would be lenient for ten to join even with less than a kazayit—and also why should we make a new dispute between them; and further Rashba who agrees with Rif regarding joining three that specifically with grain it is clear to him, also regarding joining ten he is lenient with vegetables—and such that in any case the one who joins must be obligated in some final blessing, for otherwise joining for zimun is not applicable at all—see Berachot 48; and if so in any case we require a kazayit that he be obligated in a final blessing. And that Tosefta Shibolei Leket brings as proof is not complete proof even for grain that less than a kazayit suffices, for it is possible it deals where there was a kazayit by dipping in brine, as he himself somewhat rejected there—see there.
biur-halacha/part-001.txt.2:ב: That contains a revi'it—see Beur HaGra who wrote this is Mordechai's view and as his view, and it implies his view that we do not require a revi'it; and as Beur HaGra is lenient regarding kazayit of vegetable; but I already wrote it is difficult to be lenient, for several Rishonim hold thus. And in Eliyah Rabbah he brought in the name of the book Tzedah LaDerech that even a majority of a revi'it suffices, and he wrote he did not find thus in other poskim; and in my humble opinion one should not so reject his words, since Beur HaGra and his colleagues hold we do not require a kazayit, and automatically in this too it suffices even with a very small measure—and in particular a majority of a revi'it, which is an important measure for kiddush; and there are many poskim uncertain regarding final blessing who hold the measure of a kazayit suffices for drinking, which is a third of a revi'it—and all the more so with a majority of a revi'it; and even though l'chatchila we are strict not to bless a final blessing on less than a revi'it, as stated below siman 210, nevertheless for joining it is possible to be lenient with less than this; and l'chatchila it is certainly better to be careful that he drink a revi'it, but b'dieved it is possible to be lenient.

eliyah-rabbah/part-001.txt.1:_: (1) [Levush] They are not satiated etc. Perishah greatly expanded on Levush's words that aside from his honor he was not precise—that the matter does not depend on his appetite, for certainly every person desires to eat something spiced that is good and pleasant even if he is very satiated; rather the matter depends specifically on whether he has permission, such as if they said "hav lan" etc.; and what Rif and Shulchan Aruch wrote "they can eat" means he has permission to eat—and this is clear; until here his words briefly. And I found in Semag page 110 who wrote: estimate their minds—if they did not eat so much that if they brought them delicacies and a beloved food they could still eat, he combines—until here his language. It implies explicitly like Levush's words, and so it implies in Ba'al Halachot Gedolot that certainly such is the explanation of Rif and Shulchan Aruch—and understand well.
